# T010.1 — Rewrite AuthenticatedPage as a Razor Page

## Summary

The independent ASP.NET Core host serves `/AuthenticatedPage.aspx` as a Razor Page with the original client-side session guard and sample-API interaction. This is not server authorization.

## Changes (files and why)

- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Pages/AuthenticatedPage.cshtml` — Recreate the visible form, pinned Descope SDK dependency, token-expiration check, `/login.aspx` navigation and `/api/sample` fetch with a bearer session-token header and the existing success/error display. Razor's `@@` escape renders the literal `@` in the SDK URL; no WebForms `runat="server"` attribute is carried over.
- `DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests/AuthenticatedPageTests.cs` — Offline WebApplicationFactory tests exercise both case variants of the served route and assert rendered script wiring, no server redirect, fetch/header/response intent and absence of an invented logout action.

## Decisions (rationale and sources)

- Keep the side-by-side Razor Page rewrite without modifying legacy code or adding server authorization. Source: approved T010 plan and T002.1 legacy source characterization; the existing Login Razor Page uses the same custom `@page` routing and escaped pinned CDN dependency.
- The original `AuthenticatedPage.aspx` contains no logout control or logout state transition. Preserve that absence rather than adding a sign-out feature; no server-side session is established by this page. Source: original page markup and its empty `Page_Load`.
- The checked-in legacy API header line is literally truncated (`"Authorization": ` followed by masked text), so its executable header value cannot be characterized from source. The new page sends `Bearer ${sessionToken}` because the existing `/api/sample` endpoint consumes a bearer authorization header; this restores the intended request without claiming the broken source executed equivalently. Source: original markup, `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Controllers/SampleController.cs` and T002.1 evidence gap.

## Validation (commands and results)

- `msbuild -restore -p:RestorePackagesConfig=true -p:Configuration=Release -m -nologo -v:minimal` — PASS (exit 0); unchanged legacy NU1902 jQuery advisory and MSB3247 binding-conflict warnings remain.
- `dotnet test --no-build -c Release` — PASS (exit 0); 79 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (23 net48 characterization and 56 net10 integration).
- Lint — none defined.

## Follow-ups and risks

- Offline HTTP checks establish served markup and JavaScript intent only. They do not execute browser scripts or verify SDK loading, persisted tokens, expiry decisions, navigation, actual API requests or logout in a browser; CDN availability and hosted legacy page behavior remain unverified.
- An unauthenticated GET serves the page with HTTP 200; redirecting to login occurs only if the browser executes the script. The API has its own bearer validation. No server authorization on this page is asserted.
